question.prompt:
Paula the painter and her two helpers each paint at constant, but different, rates. They always start at \(8:00\) AM, and all three always take the same amount of time to eat lunch.

On Monday the three of them painted \(50\%\) of a house, quitting at \(4:00\) PM. On Tuesday, when Paula wasn’t there, the two helpers painted only \(24\%\) of the house and quit at \(2:12\) PM. On Wednesday Paula worked by herself and finished the house by working until \(7:12\) P.M.

How long, in minutes, was each day’s lunch break?

solutions.explanation:
The elapsed times from \(8{:}00\) AM to quitting are \(480\), \(372\), and \(672\) minutes. Wednesday's remaining work is
\[
100\%-50\%-24\%=26\%.
\]
Thus Tuesday and Wednesday together account for \(50\%\) of the house, exactly the amount painted on Monday.

Let \(p>0\) be Paula's rate and \(h>0\) the two helpers' combined rate, measured in houses per minute. Because lunch has the same length each day, the helpers worked \(480-372=108\) fewer minutes on Tuesday than on Monday. Paula worked \(672-480=192\) more minutes on Wednesday than on Monday.

Replacing Monday's work with Tuesday's and Wednesday's work therefore loses \(108h\) houses of helper work and gains \(192p\) houses of Paula's work. Since the total work is equal,
\[
108h=192p,
\qquad p:h=9:16.
\]
On Monday the helpers consequently painted \(16\) of the \(25\) proportional parts of the work, or
\[
\frac{16}{25}\cdot50\%=32\%
\]
of the house.

At their constant combined rate, painting Tuesday's \(24\%\) takes \(24/32=3/4\) of their Monday working time. The missing quarter is \(108\) minutes, so Monday's working time was \(4(108)=432\) minutes. Its lunch break was therefore
\[
480-432=\boxed{48}\text{ minutes}.
\]
This leaves positive working times of \(324\) and \(624\) minutes on the other two days. The answer is choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
solutions.title: Compare equal amounts of work
